entities.name: Antonio Martín y Coll

entities.summary:
Antonio Martín y Coll (1660–1734) was a pivotal Spanish Franciscan friar, organist, and composer whose prolific transcriptions and arrangements of sacred music were instrumental in preserving and disseminating the Baroque musical heritage of the Iberian Peninsula during the early 18th century. Operating primarily within the Aragonese province of the Franciscan order, he served as a central figure in the musical life of major cathedrals and monasteries, notably the Royal Convent of Las Descalzas Reales in Madrid. His work is critical for understanding the transition of Spanish musical styles between the High Baroque and the nascent Rococo, particularly in the realm of keyboard and vocal sacred music.

Martín y Coll's most significant achievement was the compilation of several extensive manuscript collections, including the 'Flores de Música' (c. 1706–1709) and the 'Huerto de Flores' (c. 1709–1711). These monumental anthologies contain hundreds of pieces by leading Spanish and European composers of the era, such as Juan Cabanilles, Francisco Correa de Arauxo, and Girolamo Frescobaldi, alongside numerous compositions attributed to Martín y Coll himself. His meticulous efforts in copying and arranging these works, often adapting them for organ or other instruments, ensured their survival through periods of stylistic change and limited printing capabilities in Spain. He also served as maestro de capilla at the Royal Convent of Las Descalzas Reales from 1707 until his death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Antonio Martín y Coll's meticulous compilation of musical manuscripts, especially 'Flores de Música,' preserved a vast repertoire of Spanish Baroque organ and keyboard music, which otherwise would have been lost. His efforts directly shaped the understanding and performance of 17th and 18th-century Iberian music for subsequent centuries.
